title: Strike as a leverage gauge: deep in-the-money calls for core stock exposure
summary: A stock is like a call option struck at zero. The strike sets your leverage: out-of-the-money calls give a lot, deep in-the-money calls give a little with better capital efficiency. Leverage equals delta divided by the option price over the stock price; his example is about 1.72x. He uses deep ITM calls for core equity exposure.

steps.caption: The stock trades at $200. Owning it is like a call struck at zero.
Line A: 100 shares. Full capital, full downside, leverage 1x.
Line B: a deep ITM one-year call. It costs much less than the stock and still moves almost one for one.
Leverage = delta / (option price / stock price). Deep in the money it is low, about 1.7x in his example.
Breakeven is the strike plus the premium: you pay a small extrinsic cost for the efficiency.
Move the strike up and leverage rises fast. Out-of-the-money calls are the high-leverage end of the gauge.

takeaways: A stock is like a call option struck at zero.
Strike choice sets leverage: deep ITM is low leverage, OTM is high leverage.
Leverage is delta divided by option price over stock price; his example gives about 1.72x.
Deep ITM calls can be a capital-efficient core holding, not only a speculation.
caveats: The 1.72x figure comes from an example the clip does not fully show; the strike and price here are illustrative.
The call can still lose its full premium. The waitlist mention is promotional.

backtest.note: One-year deep ITM call as stock replacement, rolled with about four months left.
